title: Session Lattice Orchestrator: KV retention policy and adaptive microbatch formation for streaming chat
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Problem: Streaming chat completions create widely varying prefix lengths and write/read patterns that lead to KV cache thrashing, elevated GPU memory pressure, and high tail latency. Current continuous batcher packs by arrival window only and does not model inter-session KV reuse. This causes frequent KV spill/restore cycles and long scheduling jitter during bursts.

Proposal: Implement a Session Lattice Orchestrator (SLO) that forms microbatches by grouping sessions into transient cohorts (a lattice) based on a small feature vector: recent prefix-length distribution, estimated tokens-per-second, and observed KV hit_rate. The SLO will: 1) assign retention tier to each cohort (hot/warm/cold) and maintain a KV retention policy per-cohort; 2) drive microbatch assembly that prioritizes KV locality and latency budgets ("token-shepherd" packing); 3) implement lightweight GPU memory optimizations (in-place compressed KV placeholders, pinned CPU backing for warm/cold KV, and prefetch hints for hot cohorts).

Why different from current work: Unlike pure priority/window batchers, SLO explicitly couples cohort-aware KV retention scoring with batch formation so the cost of evicting/restoring KV is part of batch selection. This trades a small additional scheduler compute cost for reduced KV churn and more predictable GPU memory footprint.

Design highlights: - Cohort key: hash(prefix-signature, truncated-user-id, llm-model-variant) to keep cohorts stable across small prompt edits. - Retention tiers: hot (keep KV on GPU), warm (compress/pin to CPU), cold (write to tiered storage). - Eviction score: score = w1*recency + w2*predicted_hit_rate + w3*(restore_cost) where weights are tunable per-tenant. - Microbatch packing: group requests with overlapping cohort keys and similar latency budgets; within a slab, sort by remaining deadline to reduce p99. - Backpressure: when GPU memory pressure above threshold, degrade warm->cold proactively for least-benefit cohorts and enable per-request fallback to lower-quant model.

Rollout plan: start with internal runtime-1.23 on a canary queue (10% traffic) with cohorting disabled for enterprise contracts, validate no regression in p50/p95 and 20% reduction in KV restore rate before 50% rollout.

Risks and mitigations: - Scheduler CPU overhead: implement approximate scoring (sketching) and a budgeted evaluation per tick. - Incorrect cohorting might increase latency for single high-priority sessions: honor request-level priority override to bypass cohorting. - Observability gaps: add cohort_id tagging for traces and metrics immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy SLO in canary (10% of streaming chat traffic) with cohorting enabled and cohort_id in traces
Reduce KV restore ops per minute by >= 20% on canary without increasing p95 latency by > 5%
No new GPU OOMs in canary cluster for 72h under 2x peak replay
Expose metrics: cohort_count, cohort_kv_hit_rate, cohort_eviction_rate, scheduler_cpu_ms, token_shepherd_pack_efficiency
Document rollout steps and rollback path in runbook
